info.name: TalkAM API v2
info.description: TalkAM v2 API collection. v2 is a parallel lane mounted at api/v2 — v1 stays untouched. Grown section by section as endpoint shapes freeze.

formdata.description: Optional. Must exist in countries table.

request.description: Registers a user. full_name is split into first/middle/last server-side. Sends a 6-digit email verification OTP. Returns {token, user}.
Reused v1 behavior. Returns {token, user}. Re-sends a verify PIN if email is unverified.

formdata.description: Optional. true revokes every token on the account (log out everywhere); default revokes only the token this request used.

request.description: Revokes the calling device's Sanctum token (or every token, with all_devices=true). Uses the collection's bearer auth — TOKEN must be a currently-valid token. After this call that same TOKEN is dead; log in again to get a fresh one.
Reused v1 behavior. Auto-creates the user on first provider sign-in.
Public, throttled (30/min). data: {username, available}. Serves the Create Account and anonymous-mode screens.
Sends a 6-digit reset code to the email. Throttled (5/min).
Requires confirmation + strength regex; the new password must differ from the current one. The code is single-use.
Issues a 6-digit email code. Throttled (5/min); the 60s client resend countdown is covered server-side.
Verifies the 6-digit code and sets email_verified_at.
v1 me payload plus a computed data.onboarding object: {user_type, interests, avatar, consents, completed_at}. The app resumes onboarding at the first false step.
The onboarding interest chips (post_categories rows marked type=interest_topic). No parameters.
Batch interest selection from onboarding. Minimum 3 IDs; deduped server-side.
Reused v1 preset avatar list. Public.

request.description: Reused v1 profile update (also accepts name, username, gender, date_of_birth, ...).
Records onboarding intent only — role stays User.
State of all four consent keys: account_operation, session_delivery (required), anonymous_community, anonymised_research (optional).

First confirm requires both required keys true. Required keys can never be toggled off (400 — that path is account deletion). Optional keys toggle freely; revocation is go-forward (revoked_at set, granted_at preserved).
Stamps users.onboarding_completed_at and returns the derived onboarding object.
Reused v1 privacy policy content. Public.

query.description: Optional topic chip filter (id from interest-topics)

request.description: Interest-category posts first (recency-ordered), backfilled with popular recent posts. Paginated; impressions logged.
Engagement-ranked (comments + likes) over the recent 2-month window.

Reused v1 reaction toggle.
Reused v1 stats tracking (shares, engagements, clicks...).
Reused v1 stats fetch.
Gates the check-in modal: data = {checked_in, mood, checked_in_on}.
One check-in per calendar day; a same-day repeat updates the row.

Always created as pending_payment, regardless of coverage — the therapist must acknowledge (org-covered: acknowledging IS confirming, no payment needed) or the client must pay (consumer: initiate-payment then Payment Callback) before it moves to confirmed. Response includes coverage (consumer | org_bundle | org_meter | org_external) so the client UI knows whether to show a Pay button or a 'waiting on your therapist' state.
Creates a PAYMENT_FOR_SESSION payments row and returns the Flutterwave checkout payload. Retry allowed for failed bookings.
Verifies via Flutterwave then dispatches by activity. Session success -> booking confirmed + notifications; failure -> booking failed, slot freed.

Balance (ledger-derived), week/month/all-time totals, 7-day chart, stat tiles (sessions this week, avg per session, pending payout). No BVN anywhere.

item.name: W01 Business — Auth & Org Onboarding (web)
item.description:
TalkAM for Business: company signup, domain confirmation, seats/plan/bench, team invites and invited-member onboarding.

Plan: planning-docs/web-api/01-b2b-auth.md
UI: talkam-web /business/* (15 screens)

Role separation is enforced by the org.role middleware plus OrganizationPolicy / InvitationPolicy. The organization is ALWAYS derived from the caller's active membership — no endpoint accepts an organization id from the client.

Sign-in, 2FA, forgot/reset password and consent are NOT duplicated here: the web dashboard reuses the shared v2 endpoints in folders 01 and 02.

request.description: Public, admin-managed industry list for the signup form (active only, ordered). Managed in the Laravel admin under Content Management -> Industries. Headcount bands ride business/pricing-config (headcount_bands, now starting at the 1-50 band).

Seat tiers, per-seat rates, session rate, bundle options, plan features, bank details, and the LIVE network-average therapist rate. Everything the seats and plan screens render as a number comes from here. Throttled 60/min.

Creates the organization (status pending_verification), the admin user, an active admin membership, and emails a 6-digit verify_email code. Returns a Sanctum token so the wizard can continue.

Rejects free email providers (config business.blocked_email_domains) and any domain that already has a company account. Throttled 5/min.

Confirms the 6-digit code from signup. Sets users.email_verified_at AND organizations.verified_at, and flips the org to active.

Admin only. Resend uses the shared POST api/v2/auth/otp/request with type=verify_email (folder 01).
Company account + the server-computed quote for its saved choices + bench meta (chosen topics, the six selectable specialties, and the count of verified therapists serving companies). Admin only.

Persists seat count / therapist access / session bundle and returns the full quote: tier, the three monthly line items, the total, and the blended per-seat price (tier rate x network-average fairness multiplier).

Requires a confirmed domain. Rejects a seat count below seats already in use.

Stores the chosen payment method (invoice | card) and returns the plan summary and bank details. Requires a confirmed domain.

NOTE: card checkout itself is web §07 (Pricing/billing) — this only records intent.
Specialties to prioritise when onboarding therapists for this company. Optional and available before domain confirmation. Send an empty array to clear.

Parse-only: returns rows ready to invite plus per-row errors. Nothing is created.

A bad FILE (not .csv, over 5MB, unreadable) is a 422 with the deck's message; a bad ROW comes back flagged in invalid_rows so the screen can show it inline. Column order and header casing do not matter.

formdata.description: CSV with columns: email, role (employee|therapist), department

request.description:
Sends 1..n single-use invites. Each row gets a uuid, a 7-day expiry and an email.

Rejects: a role other than employee/therapist, a duplicate inside the batch, an email with a pending invite, an existing member, and anything that would exceed licensed seats (active members + pending invites). Requires a confirmed domain.

Org-scoped invite roster with status (Pending / Accepted / Cancelled) and the sent / opened / joined timestamps.

The invite uuid is NEVER returned here — it is the accept credential and only the invite email carries it. Admins resend and revoke by row id.
Extends the expiry by the configured window and re-sends the email. Pending invites only. An id belonging to another organization returns 404.
Cancels a pending invite and frees its seat. An id belonging to another organization returns 404.

What the recipient's /business/join screen shows. Deliberately minimal — company NAME, the invited email and role, nothing else — because this route is unauthenticated and enumerable by anyone holding a link. Stamps opened_at. Throttled 20/min.

Creates the member account and an ACTIVE membership with the invited role, then returns a Sanctum token.

The email and role come from the INVITATION, never from this payload — a link holder cannot enrol a different address or promote themselves. Throttled 5/min.
The six chips the web topics screen renders, in deck order, each resolved to its shared interest-topic category id (seeded by InterestTopicSeeder).

Saves interest topics for an invited member. Accepts a MINIMUM OF ONE — the web screen enables Continue at 1, while the mobile onboarding endpoint (POST api/v2/user/profile/interests) still requires 3. Both write through the same InterestService. Ids must be interest-topic categories.
The questionnaire the screen renders (4 questions x 4 options), the caller's own answers, and the derived primary concern. Employee members only — an admin gets 403.

Stores one row per category (re-taking overwrites) and returns the highest-scoring category as primary_concern, which the completion screen quotes.

PRIVACY: these individual answers are never readable by an admin. Only the company-wide aggregate (web §03) reads this table, suppressed below config('business.aggregate_minimum_cohort') respondents.

item.name: W02 Employee Dashboard (web)
item.description:
The employee (member) dashboard. Overwhelmingly REUSE — bookings (§07/§08), messaging (§16), consent (§02), privacy/notification settings (§09), reports (§10) and the notification feed are all existing endpoints and are NOT duplicated here.

Plan: planning-docs/web-api/02-employee-dashboard.md
UI: talkam-web /business/employee/* (7 screens)

Everything below is scoped to auth()->user(). None of it takes a user id, so there is no surface on which one member can read another's data — and nothing here is readable by an org admin.

request.description:
§03's endpoint, now also accepting `factors[]` and `note`.

Both new keys are OPTIONAL and use `sometimes`, so the mobile payload ({mood} alone) is unchanged AND a later mobile check-in updates the mood without wiping factors the web recorded earlier the same day. Same-day repeats update the row (one check-in per calendar day).

Factor keys are validated against config('v2.checkins.factors'); note is capped at 280 characters.
Whether today is logged, the entry itself, and the factor vocabulary the chip row renders (so the chips are config-driven, not hard-coded in the UI).
Paginated, newest first — the deck's "Recent check-ins" list. Each row carries the mood, the factor keys AND their labels, and the note.

One round-trip for both dashboard charts and both stat strips:
  streak — consecutive days ending today OR yesterday, so a streak doesn't read as broken before today's check-in is made
  days_logged / window_days, average_mood
  month_delta_percent — this month's mean vs last month's; NULL (not 0) when there is nothing to compare
  series — one entry per day with mood: null for missed days, so the chart never has to infer which day a bar belongs to
  top_factors — frequency as a percentage of the days that carried any factor

`days` is clamped to 1..366.

§07's list, unchanged, plus an additive `summary` block for the deck's four tiles: upcoming, completed, sessions_used (this quarter) and sessions_allowed.

sessions_allowed is the COMPANY's pre-purchased bundle (§01), not a per-employee quota — it is null for a direct, non-B2B member.

The "before you join" and feedback modals. Pre and post are stored independently and surface on the booking payload as the deck's 😔→🙂 pips.

Ownership goes through §07's getOwnedByUser, so another member's session 404s rather than leaking its existence.

The "Your care team" card: the therapist of the most recent active session, sessions_together, rating, and the continuity note.

PRIVACY: the note is the therapist's SHARED session note only (§11 gates sharing behind an explicit toggle). A private clinical note is never surfaced. A member with no sessions gets {"therapist": null}, not a 404.

Topic rollup for the Community tab: name, post count, one excerpt and a relative time.

ANONYMOUS BY CONSTRUCTION — no author id, username or avatar is serialized anywhere in this payload, matching the deck's "— anonymous · 2h ago". Muted (§04) and blocked (v1) authors are excluded, as are non-Active posts and categories outside the interest-topic taxonomy.

v1's FaqController registered on the v2 lane at v1's public placement. Content is seeded by EmployeeFaqSeeder (the deck's six Q&As) so the Help page is served by the API and the copy is a data change, not a deploy.

item.name: W03 Admin Dashboard (web)
item.description:
HR / Company Admin dashboard. Admin-only (org.role:admin), tenant-scoped.

Plan: planning-docs/web-api/03-admin-dashboard.md
UI: talkam-web /business/admin/* (10 screens)

THE HARD RULE: an employer sees anonymised, company-wide figures only. Every insight is wrapped as {value, cohort, suppressed} and blanked (value=null, suppressed=true) when fewer than config('business.aggregate_minimum_cohort') = 5 employees contributed. A department rollup is suppressed PER DEPARTMENT.

Three deck panels asked for individual data (a per-session table, a per-person session count, a last-active timestamp) and are NOT served — see §0 of the plan. The roster carries contract data only (seat, department, status), never behaviour.

Billing (current plan, invoices, plan catalogue) is web §07 and is not here.

request.description: KPIs (employees / active this month / sessions this month with deltas), the daily session-activity bars, top topics, the department rollup, and ROI. Every behavioural figure is suppressed below the cohort floor; seat counts are administrative and always shown.
The onboarding self-check aggregate — the pattern employees were promised HR would see 'once at least 5 people respond'. Cohort here is RESPONDENTS, not members.
The three report cards, the six-month company session trend (suppressed), and the department rollup.
Aggregate CSV — rows are months or departments, never people. A suppressed report downloads the withheld-explanation text, not the figures. Keys: usage, wellness, roi.

Active/inactive members plus pending invitations, with a stable EMP-#### id. CONTRACT DATA ONLY: id, email, department, role, status, activated_at. No session count, no last-active — those are individual behaviour.
The roster columns only (ID, Email, Department, Role, Status, Activated). No usage column.
Frees a seat. Admin seats cannot be deactivated from here. A member id from another org 404s.
Restores a seat; fails if that would exceed the licence.

Therapists available to the org, with a per-therapist company-wide month session count (withheld below the floor), plus network stats (seats/bundle used, next reset). in_network reflects the org's bench_topics.
Reports involving the org's people, ANONYMISED: category, which side of the relationship (employee/therapist), status and date — never who filed it, who it names, or the free-text description.
Administrative actions by the org's OWN admins. Employee-generated activity is excluded; one company never sees another's log.
Company name, industry, HR contact email, logo. The domain is NOT editable — it is the tenancy key.

item.name: W04 Therapist Dashboard (web)
item.description: Therapist dashboard aggregates for the frozen web UI (§04). All therapist-gated (403 for non-therapists); every client reference is anonymised ("Anonymous · #NNNN") and only therapist-authored, client-shared notes are surfaced. Earnings/profile/sessions reuse the existing therapist folders; network (non-business) therapists route here via user/me's `dashboard` field.

request.description: Greeting payload: next session (anonymised), this-week KPIs (sessions, avg rating, utilisation, completed), attention flags, continuity-of-care list (shared notes only), latest review, and employment (is_business_employed → hides Earnings). Self-care nudge appears once weekly held sessions cross the threshold.

Practice analytics over a window (?window=4w|12w|6m, default 4w): totals, completion rate, average rating + star breakdown, session volume bars, and busiest slots. All derived from this therapist's own sessions.
The recurring weekly grid — every day mapped to its ordered list of open slots. Days with no slots come back as empty arrays (day off).
Replace the whole grid in one call (delete-all + insert). A day mapped to [] turns that day off. Times are HH:MM; multiple slots per day are allowed.

Decline a pending client request (Sessions → Requests). Reuses SessionLifecycleService::cancel with the therapist as actor; the reason is never surfaced to the client. `:session` is the session UUID/id.

item.name: W05 The TalkAM Journal (web)
item.description: Public blog (§05): read-only editorial articles + newsletter capture. No auth. The index list omits `body`; the article view returns the article with `body` plus up to 3 related (same-category first). Subscribe is idempotent and throttled (5/min).

request.description: The ordered, published article list — card fields only (no `body`). The web index derives editor's-pick (first) + grid (rest) and runs search / category filtering client-side over this list.
One published article with its full `body` block array, plus a `related` array (same category first, then fill, max 3). Unknown or unpublished slug → 404.
Capture an email for the Journal newsletter band. Validates the email, throttled 5/min, idempotent (a repeat email is a plain success). Nothing is returned.

item.name: W06 Legal documents (web)
item.description: Public structured Privacy Policy / Terms of Use for the browser legal pages (§06). Reuses the existing legal tables — mobile still reads the `body` blob via user/privacy-policies; this returns the structured `document` (title, lastUpdated, callout, contact, sections). No auth, 60/min. Marketing pages (landing / for-business / for-therapists) are static editorial content with no API — see planning-docs/web-api/06-marketing-legal.md.

request.description: The structured Privacy Policy: title, last-updated, the NDPA employer-wall callout, DPO contact, and the ordered sections. Unknown slug → 404.
The structured Terms of Use: title, last-updated, (no callout), legal contact, and the ordered sections.

item.name: W07 Pricing & Billing (web)
item.description: §07. The PUBLIC pricing page reuses W01's business/pricing-config for its three rates (no new endpoint). The ADMIN billing screen is new: admin-gated + tenant-scoped via org.role — the org comes from the membership, never the client. All administrative figures (seats, plan totals, invoices); no employee data, so no cohort suppression applies.

request.description: The public pricing page's three headline rates (employee_seat_rate / therapist_access_rate / session_rate) + seat tiers + bundle options. Public, throttled 60/min. The web computes the tier cards and the worked example from these.

current_plan (label + line items + total + renewal, from the org's live quote), usage (session-bundle drawdown, seats), current_seats, and the plan catalogue (plans lite/core/plus with is_current, top-up options, seat-pack options). Admin-gated; 403 for employees/therapists.
The caller's org invoice history, newest first (id, period, seats, amount, status, tone). Tenant-scoped — another org's invoices are never returned.

Reconcile a net-terms invoice as settled (offline bank transfer) — the §08 monthly billing run issues invoices; an admin marks them paid here. Admin-gated + tenant-scoped by reference within the caller's org (404 otherwise). Returns the refreshed invoice list.

Onboarding card checkout: creates a pending payment for the up-front session-bundle charge (bundle_sessions x the ₦8,000 block rate, or the +3% ₦8,240 custom rate when bundle_custom) and returns the Flutterwave inline config {reference, amount, currency, customer, meta}. amount 0 = nothing to charge now (postpay pay-as-you-go, or no bundle). Admin-gated + org.verified. The web opens the Flutterwave inline modal with this; on success the finance/payments/callback (activity PAYMENT_FOR_BUSINESS_BUNDLE) marks the payment complete and records a paid invoice. Needs FLW_* + VITE_FLUTTERWAVE_KEY set.
